title: Boarding pass
summary: Recreate a ticket: a main part and a stub, a dashed tear line, and round notches cut into the edges.
brief: The pass is 560px wide: a white main part and a 140px orange (#f97316) stub on the right, with 12px rounded outer corners and a soft shadow that follows the whole shape (notches included).
Where the two parts meet, both have a 12px half-circle notch cut out of the top and bottom edge, and the stub has a 2px dashed white line on its left. Both parts have 24px padding.

Main part: the two airports sit at either end of a row with the arrow between them, centred vertically. Below, after a 1px #e4e4e7 line with 16px above the details and 20px above the line, four equal columns (12px apart) each show an uppercase label (0.08em spacing) over a bold value.
Stub: white text, centred both ways, 4px between lines, the seat in 36px extra bold.
hints: Lay out .pass as a grid with grid-template-columns: 1fr 140px. The details row is another grid with repeat(4, 1fr); the route row is flex with justify-content: space-between.

A notch is a transparent circle in the background: radial-gradient(circle at 100% 0, transparent 12px, #ffffff 13px) paints white everywhere except a 12px circle at the top-right corner. Use two layers, one sized to the top half and one to the bottom half.

box-shadow would ignore the notches; filter: drop-shadow(…) on .pass follows the painted shape. The stub uses the same gradients mirrored (circle at 0 0 and 0 100%) in orange, plus border-left: 2px dashed #ffffff.
solutionNotes: Two ideas carry the design. The layout is plain grid and flex: two columns for main and stub, a space-between row for the route, four equal columns for the details. The ticket shape is all background: each part paints its colour with two radial gradients, one per half, that leave a transparent circle in the corner nearest the tear line, so the notches are real holes and the page shows through. A box-shadow would still be rectangular, so the shadow is filter: drop-shadow on the whole pass, which traces whatever is painted, notches and rounded corners included.
